title: List the boundary-scan banned words in the producer brief
summary: Producers keep writing words the M19 boundary scan rejects (latest: "handoff" in a design review). I read this as adding a banned-words section to the generated producer brief. Rust builds the list from fragments, so no tracked file contains the words.

defaults_applied.how: A unit test checks that the brief names every banned word.
One focused change to the producer brief.
A test ties the brief's list to the scanner's list.
The brief text explains why the words are banned, without naming who runs Athena.
I found the scanner and the brief builder in the repository instead of asking.

assumptions: The brief is generated at runtime and stored under records/, which the scan skips, so the list can appear there. Tracked prompt files are scanned, so the list must be assembled in Rust from fragments.
Briefs for all capabilities go through producer_brief, so one change covers them.
The list is duplicated from xtask/tests/policy.rs unless xtask may depend on athena-context. The dependency-direction test probably forbids that dependency.

acceptance_criteria.text: producer_brief in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs emits a section, placed before the Checks section, that tells the producer not to write the boundary-scan words and fragments (singular, plural and hyphenated forms included) in any file, and explains that the scan is whole-word and case-insensitive.
No tracked file contains a banned term literally. The Rust source builds each term from fragments, as xtask/tests/policy.rs does, and crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md stays free of them.
A new unit test in athena-context renders a producer brief and asserts it names every word in the boundary list. Run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
The full suite passes, including athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where, and clippy is clean. Run `cargo test --locked` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`.
The word list has one stated owner, or a test fails when the brief's list and the xtask scanner's list differ. The list cannot drift silently.
The M19 row in docs/enforcement.md mentions that the producer brief lists the banned words up front. The row stays accurate and still passes the enforcement-map test.

out_of_scope: Changing the scanner's word list or the scan's behavior
Changing the reader or verifier briefs
Fixing the existing review document that failed
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference: the change needs a runtime-built list and a drift test. The reference does not account for these.
